messages:
ashley: Hey team — customer ACME (ticket CS-4521) says their Dedicated pool invoice shows ~18 reserved GPU hours on 2026-03-05 but their token/dashboard activity for that day is basically zero. They’re asking for a quick triage, repro steps, and provisional credit.

raj: Can you paste the pool_id and any sample allocation_ids? Also which invoice line (invoice id)?

ashley: Pool: pool-7f3a, acct: acme-corp, invoice: INV-2026-0305-77. I pulled a few allocation ids from the customer report: alloc-9a1, alloc-9a2, alloc-9a3.

matt: Quick PSA from an initial pass: allocations exist for that day but token counts are 0 for a lot of them. Billing stamps hours based on alloc_created_at and, crucially, we bill reserved capacity in hourly buckets (UTC). The dashboard token burn aggregates by token_end_time in the account's timezone. That mismatch + a warmup/pre-warm behavior can easily explain the delta.

jordan: I also see a pattern where healthcheck / warmup jobs spin GPUs for ~7–12 minutes and then die. Currently our billing pipeline rounds up to the nearest hour for reserved pools when an allocation crosses an hour boundary. That would make many short warmups show up as full hours on the invoice.

ashley: Can you share the queries / commands you use to repro so I can validate with the customer?

matt: Sure — to pull allocations from internal telemetry:

```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_SVC_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.redwood.com/internal/allocations?pool_id=pool-7f3a&from=2026-03-05T00:00:00Z&to=2026-03-06T00:00:00Z" \
  | jq '.allocations[] | {id: .id, created_at: .created_at, terminated_at: .terminated_at, tokens: .tokens, gpu_minutes: .gpu_minutes}'
```

And a quick reconciliation SQL I ran against the billing DB:

```
SELECT pool_id,
       allocation_id,
       date_trunc('hour', alloc_created_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS hour_utc,
       SUM(gpu_minutes)/60.0 AS billed_hours,
       SUM(tokens) AS tokens
FROM billing.allocations
WHERE pool_id = 'pool-7f3a'
  AND alloc_created_at >= '2026-03-05' AND alloc_created_at < '2026-03-06'
GROUP BY 1,2,3
ORDER BY hour_utc;
```

matt: I ran that and got 18 allocations that fall into the 03:00–04:00 UTC window with gpu_minutes ~ 8–12 each and tokens = 0. Because the billing job buckets by hour and rounds up to the hour boundary for reserved pools, we billed ~18 hours.

ashley: Confirmed on the customer side: their dashboard shows zero token events for the same times. They were surprised to be charged.

matt: Candidate root cause summary: (1) pre-warm / healthcheck instances are being charged to the reserved pool, (2) billing buckets by UTC hour while dashboard aggregates by account timezone / token_end_time, and (3) the billing pipeline currently applies an "hour-ceiling" rounding for short allocations touching an hour window. There was a related billing service change deployed 2026-02-28 that tightened hour bucketing — likely regression.

raj: Filing an internal billing incident and assigning to matt, tagging exec-billing.

matt: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) apply provisional credit to customer for 18 reserved GPU hours, 2) run a reprocess for 2026-03-05 allocations to compute pro-rated billed minutes instead of ceiling to hours, 3) patch billing service to pro-rate future allocations < 1 hour for dedicated pools, 4) add dashboard metric showing "allocations billed vs token activity" per-hour to make this visible. I’ll own 2 & 3.

billing-bot: Provisional credit issued — CR-89321 — 18.0 reserved GPU hours applied to acme-corp (INV-2026-0305-77). Customer notified.

jordan: Short repro steps we used (so support can reproduce locally):

1) Trigger a short warmup alloc via the test pool (this creates an alloc with ~10 minutes of gpu_minutes):
```
# create a test alloc (internal-only)
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"pool_id":"pool-7f3a","type":"warmup","duration_minutes":10}' \
  https://api.redwood.com/internal/allocs
```
2) Query billing allocations and check hourly bucketing using the SQL above.

matt: Follow-ups: we should backfill March 5 and recalc invoice line; if that changes invoiced amount we will issue an adjusted invoice and apply final credit. I will also add a tracer to the billing pipeline to surface when alloc.duration_minutes < 60 and was rounded up.

ashley: I told the customer we issued a provisional credit and that billing team will follow up with a final reconciliation. They asked for ETA for the patch. Matt — can you give an ETA?

matt: I can have the billing reprocess + patch ready for deployment in 48 hours, backfill running within 72 hours. Will update here when deployed.

ashley: Thanks all — please keep this thread updated so I can close the ticket with the customer. :thumbsup:
